photos.question: A client with pulmonary hypertension takes sildenafil. Which medication would make this unsafe?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #371!

⚠️ This combo can crash a blood pressure fast. Do you know which drug it is?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Isosorbide mononitrate

🧠 Rationale: Sildenafil and nitrates both dilate blood vessels.

Together they can cause severe, life-threatening hypotension.

Nitrates like isosorbide and nitroglycerin must be avoided.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Sildenafil

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 PDE-5 inhibitor

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Pulmonary arterial hypertension

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Headache and flushing

🔹 Low blood pressure

🔹 Vision changes

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Ask about all nitrate use first

✅ Check blood pressure before giving

✅ Teach to report chest pain, fainting

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Sildenafil + nitrates = BP falls off a cliff!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Before drawing an arterial blood gas from the radial artery, which test should the nurse perform?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #372!

🩸 Before you stick that radial artery, there is one quick check. Do you know it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiovascular question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Allen test

🧠 Rationale: The Allen test checks ulnar artery blood flow to the hand.

If the radial artery is injured, the ulnar artery must keep the hand perfused.

Color should return to the palm within about 5 to 15 seconds.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Allen Test

❤️ How To Do It:

🔹 Press on both radial and ulnar arteries

🔹 Client makes a fist, then opens a pale hand

🔹 Release the ulnar artery only

⚠️ Results:

🔹 Pink color returns fast: normal

🔹 Stays pale: do not use that radial site

🚨 After The ABG:

✅ Hold firm pressure 5 minutes or more

✅ Longer if on anticoagulants

✅ Put the sample on ice if required, send promptly

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Allen before artery: check the backup before you stick!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #ABG #Cardiac #NursingSkills #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Which vaccine helps protect a 70-year-old client from a common cause of bacterial pneumonia?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #373!

🫁 One shot helps protect older adults from a top cause of pneumonia. Which one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Pneumococcal vaccine

🧠 Rationale: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a leading cause of bacterial pneumonia.

Pneumococcal vaccine is recommended for older adults and high-risk clients.

The yearly flu shot also helps lower pneumonia risk.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Pneumonia Prevention

💉 Key Vaccines:

🔹 Pneumococcal vaccine

🔹 Yearly influenza vaccine

🔹 COVID-19 and RSV as recommended

⚠️ High-Risk Groups:

🔹 Older adults

🔹 Chronic heart or lung disease

🔹 Smokers and immunocompromised clients

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check vaccine history on admission

✅ Teach hand hygiene

✅ Encourage cough and deep breathing

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Pneumo-coccal = pneumonia protection!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: For most nonpregnant adults with diabetes, what is the usual hemoglobin A1C goal?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #374!

🍬 This number shows 3 months of blood sugar control. Do you know the goal?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Less than 7%

🧠 Rationale: A1C reflects average blood glucose over about 2 to 3 months.

For most nonpregnant adults with diabetes, the goal is under 7%.

Goals may be looser for older adults or clients at risk for hypoglycemia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hemoglobin A1C

🧪 Key Numbers:

🔹 Normal: under 5.7%

🔹 Prediabetes: 5.7% to 6.4%

🔹 Diabetes: 6.5% or higher

🔹 Usual treatment goal: under 7%

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ No fasting needed for the test

✅ Checked about every 3 to 6 months

✅ Lower A1C means fewer complications

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Seven is the goal: keep A1C under 7!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Endocrine #Diabetes #A1C #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Which milestone should the nurse expect in a healthy 2-year-old?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #375!

🧸 Toddler milestones show up on the NCLEX all the time. Can you spot the right one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Uses 2-word phrases

🧠 Rationale: Most 2-year-olds speak in 2-word phrases like "more milk."

Tying shoes and riding a bike come around ages 5 to 6.

Drawing a person with 6 parts is a preschool or kindergarten skill.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: 2-Year-Old Milestones

🗣️ Language:

🔹 Uses 2-word phrases

🔹 Points to things in a book

🔹 Knows about 50 words

🏃 Motor:

🔹 Runs and kicks a ball

🔹 Walks up stairs with help

🔹 Stacks about 6 blocks

🚨 When To Escalate:

✅ No 2-word phrases by 2 years

✅ Loss of skills the child had

✅ Not walking steadily

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Two years old = two-word phrases!

photos.question: On postpartum day 2, which lochia finding should the nurse expect?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #376!

🤱 Postpartum bleeding changes color over time. What is normal on day 2?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Dark red flow called lochia rubra

🧠 Rationale: Lochia rubra is dark red and lasts about 1 to 3 days.

Lochia serosa is pink-brown, from about day 4 to 10.

Lochia alba is white or yellow and can last up to 6 weeks.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Lochia Stages

🔴 Rubra:

🔹 Dark red, days 1 to 3

🩷 Serosa:

🔹 Pink-brown, days 4 to 10

⚪ Alba:

🔹 White or yellow, up to 6 weeks

🚨 When To Escalate:

✅ Soaking a pad in 1 hour

✅ Large clots

✅ Foul odor or fever

✅ Bright red flow returns after it lightened

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Red, pink, white: rubra, serosa, alba!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which finding is a negative symptom of schizophrenia?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #377!

🧠 Positive vs negative symptoms trip up so many students. Can you pick the negative one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Flat affect

🧠 Rationale: Negative symptoms are a loss of normal function.

Flat affect means little or no facial expression or emotion.

Hallucinations, delusions and disorganized speech are positive symptoms.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Schizophrenia Symptoms

➕ Positive (added):

🔹 Hallucinations

🔹 Delusions

🔹 Disorganized speech or behavior

➖ Negative (missing):

🔹 Flat affect

🔹 Lack of motivation (avolition)

🔹 Little speech (alogia)

🔹 Social withdrawal

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Build trust with short, frequent contact

✅ Encourage self-care in small steps

✅ Give meds as ordered, watch side effects

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Negative = something is missing!
